detail.title: French Energy Market
detail.sub: The context that makes the project viable — real 2024–2025 data

sections.title: WHAT IS REALLY HAPPENING
items: Not structural overproduction — it is a synchrony imbalance
Solar very productive at midday transforms the grid balance
Massive, inflexible nuclear amplifies the imbalances
1st half 2025: 32% more hours with negative prices than in 2024
May 2025: 90% of days had negative or zero prices (−€19/MWh average)

sections.title: WHEN NEGATIVE PRICES OCCUR
items: By time of day: 11h–16h (solar peak) and 2h–7h (nuclear without night demand)
By season: April–October (solar season)
1st half: 2× more negative-price hours than the 2nd half
Record: 31 March 2025 at 13:30 — solar production reached 18 GW

sections.title: THE FRENCH DUCK CURVE
items: EDF shut down 6 nuclear reactors on 24–25 Nov. 2024 due to wind record (19.3 GW)
First time in history that 6 reactors are shut down due to excess supply
Shows that even "inflexible" nuclear must yield to oversupply

sections.title: PPA MARKET IN FRANCE
items: 2025: PPA market grows from 600 MW to over 1,200 MW of contracted capacity
Active corporate buyers: Orange, Carrefour, SNCF, Les Mousquetaires, Leroy Merlin
Huge gap: PPA market for SMEs is underdeveloped — there is the opportunity
End of ARENH (Dec. 2025): mechanism that allowed buying nuclear at €42/MWh
With ARENH gone, buyers urgently seek private PPA alternatives

detail.title: Negative Prices — The Raw Material
detail.sub: Electricity nobody wants — and it grows every year

sections.title: WHEN THEY OCCUR
items: By hour: 11h–16h (solar peak) and 2h–7h overnight (nuclear with no demand)
By season: April–October (solar + nuclear + low heating demand)
First half: 2× more negative hours than the second
Q2 2024: +10% of time at negative price — in that quarter alone
Record: 31 March 2025 at 13:30 — unprecedented solar peak of 18 GW

sections.title: WHAT THIS MEANS FOR ANY SOLUTION
items: Those hours are the raw material: free electricity or paid to consume it
Any process that can switch on and off in those windows has a structural advantage
The trend is clear: more negative hours every year — the opportunity grows on its own

detail.title: The French Duck Curve
detail.sub: Why the problem worsens structurally every year

sections.title: WHAT IT IS
items: Duck-shaped curve: solar production rises at noon, demand falls → price collapses
French nuclear (67% of the mix) is inflexible: hard to switch off and on
Result: at noon there is structural surplus the system cannot absorb quickly

sections.title: RECENT EVIDENCE
items: November 2024: EDF shut down 6 reactors in 3 days due to wind record (Storm Bert, 19.3 GW) — first time in history
It was not the wind replacing the reactors: there was too much energy and nobody to sell it to at a profitable price
April 2024: EDF modulated reactors due to negative prices linked to renewables
RTE estimates that by 2030 HEMS could reduce curtailment by 75%

sections.title: WHY IT WORSENS
items: Each new GW of solar installed adds more negative-price hours at noon
France installed +5 GW solar in 2024 (total: 25.3 GW) — the trend does not stop
The problem is not solar energy: it is the lack of local flexible sinks

detail.title: Business Model
detail.sub: 4 uncorrelated revenue streams — the key argument for investors

sections.title: WHY 4 UNCORRELATED STREAMS
items: Most renewable projects have a single source: spot electricity price
If the price drops or goes negative, the model collapses
With 4 uncorrelated streams: if one falls, the others compensate
In financial terms: cash flow diversification → lower risk → better valuation

children.label: 10.1 Water sales
children.sub: Water PPA · fixed price · guaranteed demand

detail.title: Water Sales
detail.sub: First revenue stream — the most stable

sections.title: CUSTOMERS
items: Households and residences in summer water-scarce areas (Occitanie, PACA)
SMEs: restaurants, hotels, agriculture, light industry
Municipalities supplementing their public network

sections.title: PRICING MODEL
items: Fixed-price contract per m³, similar to a PPA but for water
Term: 5–15 years — the client knows exactly what they pay
Water prices in France have risen consistently — attractive for the client

sections.title: COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE
items: Water has guaranteed demand regardless of energy price
Tank storage: decouples production from consumption (days or weeks)
A battery stores electricity for hours — a tank stores the energy equivalent for weeks at near-zero cost

detail.title: Grid Flexibility (RTE)
detail.sub: Second stream — RTE pays for consuming during surplus moments

sections.title: WHAT IT IS EXACTLY
items: RTE (Réseau de Transport d'Électricité) pays actors who can switch their consumption on or off on demand
Called "adjustment services" or "effacement"
Register as a flexible consumer; when RTE has excess production, they activate you and pay you to consume

sections.title: THE DOUBLE GAIN
items: RTE pays you for consuming the electricity
You convert that electricity into water (or another product) that you also sell
Two revenue streams from the same action: consuming solar surplus

sections.title: CRITICAL STAKEHOLDER
items: ⚠️ RTE can cut your production if the grid is saturated and you have no agreement
⚠️ Their technical validation as a "certified flexible load" opens the adjustment services market
Without their cooperation the model fails — with it they pay you to exist

detail.title: Carbon Credits
detail.sub: Third stream — recurring, predictable, improves the ESG story

sections.title: HOW THEY ARE GENERATED
items: The installation replaces methods that consume fossil energy or require carbon-intensive infrastructure
Each m³ of water produced with solar energy displacing conventional water has a calculable, certifiable carbon footprint
Absorbing solar surpluses that would otherwise be curtailed avoids wasting that energy

sections.title: STRATEGIC VALUE
items: Not the main revenue — but recurring and predictable
Greatly improves the ESG story for investors
Relevant certifications: Label Bas Carbone, Guarantees of Origin, ISO 14001

detail.title: Salt and Minerals
detail.sub: Fourth stream — turns the only waste into a product

sections.title: WHAT IS OBTAINED
items: Reverse osmosis brine contains crystallisable salt, magnesium, potassium and lithium
Instead of being a waste management cost, it becomes a saleable product
France has an established salt industry (Guérande, Camargue) — existing market and local know-how

sections.title: INVESTOR NARRATIVE VALUE
items: The message: "We have no waste, we have four products"
Turns the model into virtually waste-free (ZLD)
In MVP phase: diluted brine returned to sea under certified environmental protocol
At scale: crystallising and selling the salt adds a fourth income stream without changing the core process

children.label: 11. Competitors and Allies

detail.title: Competitors and Allies

sections.title: STRATEGIC MAP
items: Demand flexibility / effacement: direct competitor (Enerdigit, Orus Energy)
Stationary batteries: indirect competitor (Ze Energy)
V2G electric vehicles: long-term threat (DREEV/EDF, EVVE Project)
Green hydrogen: institutional competitor (Air Liquide + TotalEnergies, Hyd'Occ)

sections.title: STRATEGIC CONCLUSION
items: No actor in France is combining distributed solar + local production + PPA for SMEs and residences
That space is empty — first-mover window
The closest is in Saudi Arabia (DESOLINATION) or Spain/Morocco

detail.title: Demand Flexibility (Effacement)
detail.sub: The principle: pay companies to consume more during surplus moments

sections.title: MAIN PLAYERS
items: Enerdigit (Nantes): most relevant startup in this space, 20 employees, >€20M revenue 2024, industrial grid flexibility solutions
Orus Energy (GreenTech Innovation 2024): helps and compensates commercial buildings for smart consumption management
Ecojoko: connected assistant for individuals, makes real-time consumption visible

sections.title: RELEVANCE TO THE PROJECT
items: Producing any product (water, H₂, etc.) as a "flexible load" is exactly this model
Enerdigit and Orus are direct competitors in capturing companies as "flexible sinks"
The difference: the project produces something physical (water, H₂…), they only adjust consumption

detail.title: Stationary Battery Storage
detail.sub: Indirect competitor — they store energy, the project converts it into a product

sections.title: PLAYERS
items: Ze Energy (founded 2019): designs, builds and operates hybrid solar + storage plants, funded by Amundi Transition Énergétique
STEP (pumped storage stations): ~5 GW turbined + 4.3 GW pumped in France by end 2024
Public investment: EC validated €1.3bn in France for short-term non-carbon flexibility solutions

sections.title: PROJECT ADVANTAGE OVER BATTERIES
items: A battery stores electricity for hours — a water tank stores the energy equivalent for days or weeks
No losses, no degradation, at near-zero cost
It is the cheapest "storage" that exists — nobody in the energy market is looking at it this way

detail.title: V2G — Electric Vehicles as Storage
detail.sub: One of the best-funded solutions in France — long-term threat

sections.title: PLAYERS
items: DREEV (EDF + Nuvve): RTE certified their participation, implements V2G in companies and local authorities
EVVE Project (EDF + European Innovation Fund): 800 bidirectional charging stations, virtual battery of 8.36 MW

sections.title: LONG-TERM POTENTIAL
items: EVs connected home + work could reduce up to 92% of the need for stationary battery storage
By 2040: potential savings of up to €4.4bn annually
RTE already anticipates this in its "rapid decarbonisation" scenarios

sections.title: RELEVANCE TO THE PROJECT
items: Short term (2-month MVP): V2G still in pilot phase, does not cover the gap
Long term: if millions of cars become mobile batteries, need for other sinks decreases
Project advantage: produces something physical with guaranteed demand — V2G does not produce water

detail.title: Green Hydrogen (Power-to-Gas)

sections.title: MAIN PLAYERS

sections.title: BUT THERE IS AN IMPORTANT BRAKE
items: Cour des comptes: new H₂ production targets "still appear out of reach"

H₂ distribution infrastructure nonexistent — must be built from scratch

sections.title: KEY ARGUMENT FOR INVESTORS
items: Where green H₂ needs €9bn of public funding to start, the project can operate with existing infrastructure
H₂ has no market at scale today — water has had a functioning market for centuries

detail.title: Export — The Status Quo
detail.sub: The French State's current emergency response

sections.title: WHAT IT IS
items: When there is too much electricity, France exports it to Germany, Spain, Italy or Switzerland
The problem: when supply exceeds demand, prices go negative
Producers must "pay to export" their electricity
2024: France exported a record 90–101 TWh, but generating losses when prices were negative

sections.title: RELEVANCE TO THE PROJECT
items: Export is the status quo the project displaces
The investor narrative: exporting at negative price is a loss of value
The project converts that loss into a locally saleable product

items: "We don't sell door to door. We sign a contract with whoever already has the problem, and from there we reach thousands of end users without touching them one by one."

sections.title: 3-PHASE MODEL
items: Phase 1 — MVP (2 months): 1 solar producer in Occitanie or PACA, surplus at zero price, prove the model works
Phase 2 — B2B Scale: more producers, product sold to municipalities and local industry — not to individual households yet

sections.title: PRIORITY CLIENTS
items: Municipalities: supplement their public network with fixed-price water under PPA

sections.title: WHY MUNICIPALITIES FIRST
items: B2B decision — one contract with the municipality gives access to the entire population

Local political support = land permits + lower regulatory friction

detail.title: Phase 3 — Residential
detail.sub: Only when there is volume, brand and regulatory validation

sections.title: WHY NOT START WITH HOUSEHOLDS
items: Very long sales cycle: each household is an individual decision — can take 6 to 18 months to sign
Small ticket: a household consumes little — you need thousands for viable volume
Very high acquisition cost: advertising, visits, demos, follow-up — all for a small contract
Market education from zero: the average household does not know about solar overproduction or PPAs

sections.title: WHEN RESIDENTIAL MAKES SENSE
items: When you have a B2B success case certifying the technical and economic model
When you have a recognised brand that reduces per-household acquisition cost
When you have regulatory validation that removes entry barriers

sections.title: THE CENTRAL INSIGHT
items: "France has too much energy exactly when nobody wants it, and too little of what that energy could produce."
The problem is not that energy is scarce — the problem is that it is surplus at the wrong moment and nobody knows how to turn it into something useful

sections.title: IN ONE PHRASE FOR INVESTORS
items: "We are the only company that converts France's problem —electricity nobody wants— into the resource France will need most: water."

children.label: 13.1 The central insight

detail.title: The Central Insight
detail.sub: The second layer of the insight — why it is truly defensible

sections.title: WHY WATER AND NOT SOMETHING ELSE
items: Water has 3 properties no other product has simultaneously:
① Guaranteed demand regardless of energy price
② Cheap storage for days or weeks in simple tanks
③ A market that already exists with known distribution infrastructure

sections.title: ADVANTAGE OVER GREEN H₂
items: H₂ also converts surpluses into a product, but needs new infrastructure, very high storage costs, and its market does not yet exist at scale
You are not inventing a market — you are entering one that has been working for centuries

sections.title: THE QUESTION THAT LEAVES INVESTORS SPEECHLESS
items: "Do you know any other business where your main raw material —electricity— sometimes has a negative price, meaning they pay you to consume it, and you still produce something you can sell?"
That is the essence of the model. The honest answer: no, nothing like it exists in France today
